children.name: Hallopora elegantula
children.description: Hallopora is an extinct genus of bryozoans of the family Halloporidae, first identified from the Lower Silurian period. They can be found in Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky of the Midwestern United States, commonly in the Ordovician Kope Formation.

children.name: Tarphophragma macrostoma
children.description: Ramose colonies, branch diameter 3.0 - 3.6 mm. Exozone distinct, 0.5 - 0.6 mm wide, endozone 2.0 - 2.4 mm wide. Autozooecia long, growing parallel to branch axis for a long distance in endozone and bending sharply in exozone, having rounded-polygonal shape in transverse section in endozone. Autozooecial apertures oval to polygonal. Autozooecial diaphragms thin, planar, widely spaced in endozone; common to abundant in exozone, planar, rarely inclined, developed as extension of wall cortex. Mesozooecia arising in endozone, polygonal in transverse section, 2 - 6 surrounding each autozooecial aperture. Mesozooecial diaphragms planar, densely spaced. Acanthostyles absent. Autozooecial walls indistinctly laminated, 0.005 - 0.008 mm thick in endozone; displaying distinct reverse V-shaped structure with dark autozooecial boundary, with weakly developed wall cortex continued in diaphragms, 0.04 - 0.12 mm thick in exozone. Maculae indistinct, consisting of macrozooecia. COMPARISON
